HeapLocalBucketReuse: Different lifetimes: Stark frees each Box per iteration; C/Rust hold batches of up to 128 (Rust also builds a Vec).
SystemMemoryBucketReallocate: Stark allocates/reallocates/frees but never writes/reads allocation payload. C/Rust write a byte and verify preservation after each shrink; Rust initially zero-initializes Vec.
SystemMemoryFallbackReallocate: Stark never writes/reads allocation payload. C/Rust write and verify a byte; Rust zero-initializes and extends Vec whereas C reallocates uninitialized storage.
MemoryDynamicReserveGrowth: Same fixed append/fill/checksum scenario; language library capacity/zero-initialization and append implementations differ.
DictionaryLookup: Canonical Rust uses randomized std HashMap; C uses its benchmark-specific table and Stark its Dictionary. Results include hashing/table policy differences.
DictionaryMixed: Same logical operation sequence and final checks; canonical Rust randomized HashMap differs from C custom and Stark dictionary policy.
LinkedListReservedPush: Stark and C reserve node storage; Rust std::collections::LinkedList has no node-reservation API and allocates nodes individually.
ConsoleWrites: Canonical immediate Stark versus buffered C stdout; also differing literal contents/encoding. Report output byte/hash checks; keep distinct from matched buffered benchmark.
ConsoleWritesBuffered: Matched explicit stdout buffering with immediate stderr; exact output hashes are checked in preflights.
DirectoryEnumeration: Same 128 entries and 128 enumerations; Rust constructs path Strings and converts file-name OsStrings, C and Stark use different directory APIs; setup/cleanup included.
FileSystemPathTranscode: Includes different I/O batching, UTF-16 construction and path/metadata work across implementations; not a pure transcoder throughput test.
TextParsing: C volatile inputs and Rust black_box preserve primitive parses; Stark constant literals fold some primitive parsing. Stark wide parsers use UTF-32 while C/Rust parse bytes.
TextConcatCopy: Library growth, encoding/storage and allocation strategies differ; interpret as canonical program comparison.
PathRepeatedSmallOps: Constant paths permit dead-payload/scan folding; retain Stark fallible reserve and cleanup. Constant-input startup comparisons are not dynamic path throughput.
ConstantIntegerFormatting: Native Stark main is xor eax,eax; ret: all constant formatting/checksum work folds away. C/Rust retain runtime formatting, including 1024-bit decimal conversion; this is constant specialization plus startup, not dynamic-formatting throughput.
UnicodeFormatting: Stark precomputes the constant wide-number outputs but main is not return-only: native code retains a TextError formatter call and two memcpy sites. C retains calls to its wide-number formatter, and Rust retains formatting-framework work. This measures constant specialization and differing library paths, not general dynamic-formatting throughput.
AsciiToUnicodeConversionTinyLiteral: Constant two-byte input and repeated edge-unit checksum permit complete kernel elimination; native inspection distinguishes startup from retained conversion work.
AsciiToUnicodeLargeLiteralSpecialization: Constant 64-byte input and edge-unit checksum permit literal specialization and kernel elimination; not dynamic transcoder throughput.
AsciiToUnicodeConversion: Constant input; some or all conversion/checksum work can fold.
AsciiToUnicodeWideningKernel: Constant manual widening; some or all widening/checksum work can fold.
PathFacts: Constant paths; scans can fold, with remaining checksum work varying by compiler.
PathQueries: Constant paths; query/scanning and checksum work can fold.
AbstractionHandWritten: Runtime PID-seeded arithmetic recurrence; compare retained native work rather than source operation counts.
BitwiseRangePruning: Range-typed Stark inputs expose proved bounds; canonical C/Rust rely on inferred bounds. All use PID-seeded arithmetic.
AlgebraicIdentitySimplification: Algebraic identities can fold, while the PID-seeded recurrence remains.
StackNestedFieldForwarding: Small stack field operations can fold; runtime PID/checksum recurrence distinguishes it from memory throughput.
StackScalarLoadForwarding: Small stack scalar operations can fold; runtime PID/checksum recurrence remains.
DirectCallInlining: Small direct helper calls may inline/fold; runtime PID/checksum recurrence remains.
